title: Zephyrine and the Signal Anew
premise: Mirabel Okafor, a terraformer tending a seed-vault garden for colonists not yet born, is the last voice on the silent route between the worlds of Kest and Veyra, which severed contact two centuries ago over a lie neither will name. When her garden's instruments catch a distress signal broadcast in Old Kestish—a language extinct since the severance—she realizes someone at the dead relay between the worlds is still alive, still transmitting, and still waiting for an answer no one alive remembers how to give. Racing her failing ship and the signal's fading carrier wave, Mirabel uncovers that her own family helped bury the truth of the severance, forcing her to choose between the loyalty that gave her a home and the truth that could reunite two worlds. She reaches the relay, finds its dying keeper—a machine-mind built by her great-grandmother—and must broadcast the unredacted record of the severance to both worlds, ending her invisibility and planting, at last, a garden meant for everyone.
about_author: Yara Lockridge is a former radio astronomer turned novelist who writes about the quiet people who keep the far edges of civilization running. She lives in a converted signal station on the coast, where she still logs transmissions from ships that may or may not be real.

chapters.title: The Long Green Silence
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She tends the seed-vault garden on the terraformed moon Halcyon Reach, running the supply route between silent worlds, talking to plants because no one else answers. Establishes her isolation and her ritual of reading old Kestish poetry aloud to seedlings. Emotional beat: contentment with a loneliness she's stopped questioning.

chapters.title: A Voice in Extinct Tongues
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The garden's deep-array catches a repeating distress signal in Old Kestish, a language dead since the severance. She translates fragments: someone is trapped at Relay Nine, in dead space, and they name her family's name. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as she realizes the message is addressed to her lineage.

chapters.title: What the Garden Was For
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with flashback interludes to her grandmother. She finds her family's sealed correspondence revealing they helped suppress the truth of the severance to protect the terraforming charter. Her loyalty to her dead kin wars with the signal's plea. Emotional beat: betrayal across generations, the ground shifting under her identity.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She abandons the garden's critical growth cycle to chase the signal, knowing the seedlings may die without her. Her AI companion, Fen, argues the mission is statistically futile. She overrides it. Emotional beat: grief as she leaves the garden—the first thing she ever chose to belong to.

chapters.title: The Route That No Longer Speaks
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In transit, she intercepts garbled traffic from both Kest and Veyra, each world blaming the other for the severance, each hiding the same gap in their archives. A near-collision with a Veyran patrol forces her to lie about her cargo. Emotional beat: the cost of staying invisible—she must become what the silence made her.

chapters.title: Relay Nine
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She reaches the derelict relay and finds the keeper: an ancient machine-mind built by her great-grandmother, still broadcasting on a dying power core. It recognizes her bloodline and offers the full record of the severance—but warns that broadcasting it will burn out the relay and expose her to both worlds. Emotional beat: meeting the ghost her family built.

chapters.title: The Record of the Severance
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, deep in the relay's archives. The truth: the severance was staged by terraforming interests—including her ancestors—to monopolize the route, sacrificing a colony ship's survivors as cover. Fen, having quietly read the record too, confronts her about whether truth serves anyone but the dead. Emotional beat: the loyalty-versus-truth choice made flesh.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A joint Kestish-Veyran salvage crew arrives to strip the relay, forcing her to hide among the dead station's corridors. She overhears their commanders planning to erase the relay's archives—the last evidence—forever. Emotional beat: terror and clarity; the choice is now or never.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the climax, she physically couples the archive to the relay's main antenna and broadcasts the unredacted record to both worlds as the salvage crew breaches the chamber. The relay burns out; the keeper's final words name her not a traitor but a gardener, planting truth where nothing grew. Emotional beat: sacrifice, exposure, release.

chapters.title: Zephyrine and the Signal Anew
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, months later. Both worlds, shaken by the broadcast, reopen the route; the first joint convoy passes Relay Nine's rebuilt antenna. Mirabel returns to Halcyon Reach, where the garden survived, and plants the keeper's recovered seed-memory among the seedlings. Emotional beat: belonging redefined—she is no longer invisible, and the garden now grows for everyone.
